records.name: Gotoku-ji Temple
records.description: A Soto Zen temple founded in 1480 that served as the Ii clan's family temple during the Edo period. It is popularly regarded as the birthplace of the maneki-neko (beckoning cat), and its grounds hold thousands of small cat figurines donated by visitors near the temple's pagoda and the Ii clan mausoleum.

tips.text: The temple is a roughly 5-minute walk from Miyanosaka Station on the Tokyu Setagaya Line, or about 10 minutes from Gotokuji Station on the Odakyu Line.

records.station: Miyanosaka Station (Tokyu Setagaya Line), about 5 min walk

records.name: Kuhonbutsu Joshin-ji Temple
records.description: A Jodo-sect Buddhist temple founded in 1678 by the priest Kaseki on the former grounds of Okusawa Castle. It takes its popular name, Kuhonbutsu ("nine Buddhas"), from nine gilded Amida Buddha statues housed across three halls, each representing a different level of rebirth in the Pure Land.

tips.text: The temple gate opens at 6:00 and closes at 4:30pm; phone inquiries are handled 9:00-16:00.

records.name: Mangan-ji (Todoroki Fudoson)
records.description: A Shingon-shu Chisan-ha temple claiming Heian-period origins, revived in 1470 as a chapel for the outlying Todoroki Castle fortification of Setagaya Castle and relocated to its present site in the mid-1500s. Its subsidiary chapel above Todoroki Valley, known locally as Todoroki Fudoson, enshrines a Fudo Myoo image and is the 17th stop on the Kanto region's 36 Fudo temple pilgrimage.

records.name: Todoroki Valley
records.description: A roughly 1km wooded ravine along the Yazawa River at the southern edge of the Musashino Plateau, one of the few valley landscapes remaining within Tokyo's built-up area. A walking trail follows the river through zelkova, konara oak, and dogwood trees, taking about 20-30 minutes to walk end to end.

tips.text: Entry point is down the steps at Golf Bridge, about a 3-minute walk from Todoroki Station on the Tokyu Oimachi Line.
The valley's walking trail was closed for tree-trimming work as of May 2024, with reopening scheduled by March 2026; check Setagaya City's official website before visiting.

records.station: Todoroki Station (Tokyu Oimachi Line), about 3 min walk
records.address: 等々力渓谷公園, 等々力, 世田谷区, 東京都, 日本

records.name: Setagaya Boro-ichi Flea Market
records.description: A twice-yearly flea market held since 1578 along Boroichi-dori street, designated one of Tokyo's Intangible Folk Cultural Properties. Around 700 stalls sell antiques, used clothing, plants, toys, and daily goods; the name comes from "boro" (old fabric scraps), the market's original trade goods.

tips.text: Held only on December 15-16 and January 15-16 each year, 9:00-20:00; the street centers on the Setagaya Daikan Yashiki.
Many visitors buy daikan mochi, a freshly made rice cake sold by market vendors.

records.station: Kamimachi Station or Setagaya Station (Tokyu Setagaya Line)

records.name: Shimokitazawa Ichibangai Shopping Street
records.description: A shopping street near Shimokitazawa Station's east exit with a dense concentration of cafes, second-hand clothing stores, record shops, live music venues, and inexpensive izakaya bars, reflecting the neighborhood's independent, laid-back retail character.
records.station: Shimo-Kitazawa Station (Inokashira Line or Odakyu Odawara Line), East Exit, 5 min on foot

records.name: Shimokitazawa
records.description: A bohemian district in western Setagaya known for vintage clothing stores, independent bookshops, record shops, and a live-music scene, with a more laid-back feel than youth-culture hubs like Harajuku or Shibuya. Newer additions include the Mikan Shimokita complex and Reload, built along the former Odakyu rail alignment.
records.station: Shimokitazawa Station (Odakyu Line and Keio Inokashira Line)
records.address: 下北沢, 北沢二丁目, 北沢, 世田谷区, 東京都

records.name: Sangenjaya
records.description: A commercial and residential district ('Sancha') that takes its name from three Edo-period tea houses (Shigaraki, Sumiya, and Tanakaya) that stood at a road junction during the temple-pilgrimage boom, a name already common by the early 1800s. It became a designated place name in 1932 and today retains retro shopping alleys such as Eko Nakamise and Suzuran Street alongside the Carrot Tower complex.
records.station: Sangen-jaya Station (Tokyu Den-en-toshi Line and Setagaya Line)
records.address: 三軒茶屋, 世田谷区, 東京都, 日本

records.name: Carrot Tower (Sky Carrot Observation Deck)
records.description: A 26-story mixed-use high-rise completed in November 1996, directly connected to Sangen-jaya Station. Its top floor houses the free 'Sky Carrot' observation area with 360-degree views including Mt. Fuji on clear days; the building also contains offices, shops, a broadcasting studio for FM Setagaya, and the Setagaya Public Theatre.
records.station: Sangen-jaya Station (Tokyu Den-en-toshi Line and Setagaya Line), integrated into the building

records.name: Setagaya Public Theatre
records.description: A public performing-arts venue inside Carrot Tower, opened in 1997 and funded by Setagaya City. It comprises a 600-seat main theatre and a smaller 225-seat space called Theatre Tram, focused on contemporary drama and dance alongside community participation programs.
records.station: Sangen-jaya Station (Tokyu Den-en-toshi and Setagaya lines)

records.name: Setagaya Art Museum
records.description: A museum opened in 1986 on the grounds of Kinuta Park, designed by architect Shozo Uchii. Its permanent collection exceeds 18,000 works by local and international artists, shown alongside rotating exhibitions, concerts, film screenings, and workshops across the main building and three annexes.

tips.text: Last entry is 30 minutes before closing; the museum is closed Mondays and New Year holidays (if a Monday closure falls on a public holiday, it closes the following day instead).

records.station: Yoga Station (Den-en-toshi Line, North Exit), about 17 min on foot

records.name: Kinuta Park
records.description: A 39-hectare public park opened in 1957 on the site of a former public golf course, of which about 24 hectares is grassland. It is known for cherry blossom viewing, with Someiyoshino, yamazakura, and yaezakura varieties extending the hanami season to over two weeks, plus a bird sanctuary, a 1.66km cycling course, and the Setagaya Art Museum.

tips.text: The cycling course doubles as a walking course outside the hours of 9:00-16:00.

records.station: Yoga Station (Den-en-toshi Line), about 20 min on foot; Seijogakuen-mae Station (Odakyu Odawara Line)

records.name: Setagaya Park
records.description: A municipal park with sports facilities including baseball fields, tennis courts, a skate park, and a summer swimming pool, plus a large fountain and promenade. The park displays a statically preserved D51-class steam locomotive (D51 272) alongside a children's play area.

tips.text: The preserved D51 272 locomotive sits within the park.

records.station: Ikejiri-ohashi Station or Sangen-jaya Station (Den-en-toshi Line), about 18 min on foot
records.address: 世田谷公園, 鮫洲大山線, 池尻一丁目, 池尻, 世田谷区

records.name: Hanegi Park
records.description: A recreational park near Shimokitazawa with a racetrack, tennis courts, and wooden climbing play structures, popular with families and dog owners for its grassy open space. It is known for approximately 650 plum trees that bloom between January and March.

tips.text: Around 650 plum trees bloom in the park between January and March.

records.station: Umegaoka Station (Odakyu Line), about 5 min on foot

records.name: Setagaya Literary Museum
records.description: A museum founded in April 1995 and operated by the Setagaya Cultural Foundation, dedicated to modern literature connected to Setagaya. Its holdings exceed 100,000 items, including handwritten manuscripts and correspondence from authors, with recent exhibitions often featuring manga artists.
records.station: Roka-koen Station (Keio Line), South Exit, about 5 min on foot

records.name: Gotoh Museum
records.description: A private museum in the Kaminoge district opened in 1960 to display the collection of Keita Goto, chairman of the Tokyu Group. The collection centers on classical Japanese and Chinese art, including paintings, calligraphy, crafts, and archaeological objects, several designated National Treasures or Important Cultural Properties, most notably sections of the 12th-century illustrated handscroll of The Tale of Genji. The museum grounds include a garden with a tea house and ponds.

tips.text: The Tale of Genji handscroll sections are typically shown only in a limited display during the first week of May.

records.station: Kaminoge Station (Oimachi Line, North Exit), about 5 min on foot

records.name: Setagaya Hachimangu Shrine
records.description: A Shinto shrine founded in 1091 when the samurai commander Minamoto no Yoshiie, delayed in Setagaya by heavy rain, held a ceremony for the Hachiman deity and wrestled sumo with his subordinates, an event said to have started the shrine's dedicated sumo tradition. Its dohyo (sumo ring) still hosts a ritual sumo tournament during the autumn festival, historically counted among the Edo period's three great suburban sumo events alongside Shibuya Hikawa Shrine and Oi Kashima Shrine.

records.name: Setagaya Daikan Yashiki
records.description: The former official residence of the Oba family, who served as daikan (magistrates) for the area during the mid-Edo period. Designated a Tokyo Metropolitan historic site in 1952 and a National Important Cultural Property in 1978, it is notable for its large wooden thatched roof and free public access to its earthen-floored entrance hall, which displays preserved tools and fixtures.

tips.text: Indoor exploration is only permitted during staffed hours, 13:00-16:00; access may be restricted in summer (June-September) or during events.

records.station: Kamimachi Station (Tokyu Setagaya Line), about 3 min on foot

records.name: Setagaya Local History Museum
records.description: A local history museum on the grounds of the Setagaya Daikan Yashiki, opened in September 1964 and designed by architect Kunio Maekawa. It exhibits materials on Setagaya's history and culture, including excavated pottery, tumulus models, and items related to Ii Naosuke.

records.name: Tokyu Setagaya Line
records.description: A 5km, 10-station light-rail tramway operated by Tokyu Corporation between Sangen-jaya and Shimo-takaido, opened January 18, 1925 as a branch of the former Tamagawa Line. Governed under Japan's Tramways Act and running on a distinctive 1,372mm gauge, it is one of only two tram lines remaining in Tokyo (the other being the Toden Arakawa Line) and runs some cars in a maneki-neko livery.

tips.text: Stations in order: Sangen-jaya, Nishi-taishido, Wakabayashi, Shoin-jinja-mae, Setagaya, Kamimachi, Miyanosaka, Yamashita, Matsubara, Shimo-takaido.

records.address: 東急電鉄世田谷線, 経堂本町通り, 宮坂一丁目, 宮坂, 世田谷区

records.name: Kitazawa Hachiman Shrine
records.description: A shrine in the Daizawa neighborhood with roots dating to the Bunmei era (1469-87), founded at the request of the Kira family who then lorded over Setagaya Castle. Traditionally the guardian shrine for northern Setagaya, it was the area's community center before Shimokitazawa Station opened in 1927 shifted the local hub about a kilometer north. The current reinforced-concrete shrine building dates to 1978, with a torii gate erected in 1963.
records.address: 北澤八幡神社, 森巌寺川緑道, 代沢三丁目, 代沢, 世田谷区

records.name: Kuhonbutsugawa Ryokudo (Green Promenade)
records.description: A roughly 1.6km landscaped greenway built over the Kuhonbutsu River after it was channeled underground in 1974. The path runs behind Joshin-ji Temple (the Kuhonbutsu temple) in Setagaya before crossing into Jiyugaoka in Meguro and joining the Nomi River near Midorigaoka Station; the stretch near the temple functions mainly as a residential walkway.

records.name: Futakotamagawa Park
records.description: A riverside park opened in 2013 beside the Tama River, near Futako-Tamagawa Station and the Futako Tamagawa Rise shopping complex. It includes the landscaped Japanese garden Kishin-en, a toddler playground, a grassy picnic area, and a lookout point with views toward the Tanzawa mountains and Mt. Fuji on clear days.
records.station: Futako-tamagawa Station (Tokyu Den-en-toshi Line), about 9 min on foot

records.name: Sakura Jingu Shrine
records.description: A small shrine in the Shinmachi neighborhood known for early-blooming kawazu-zakura cherry trees, typically flowering from mid-February to early March, ahead of Tokyo's main cherry blossom season. Visitors can buy pink ribbons from the shrine office to tie to the large sakura trees flanking the main hall.

tips.text: Kawazu-zakura at the shrine bloom earlier than most of Tokyo, roughly mid-February to early March.

records.station: Sakura-Shinmachi Station (Tokyu Den-en-toshi Line), about 3 min on foot

records.name: Komazawa Olympic Park
records.description: A 413,537 sq m sports park built for the 1964 Summer Olympics, on the site of the former Tokyo Golf Club. About 90% of the park lies within Setagaya, with the remainder in Meguro. It contains the Komazawa Olympic Park Stadium, Komazawa Gymnasium, and additional soccer, baseball, swimming, tennis, jogging, and cycling facilities.
records.address: 駒沢オリンピック公園総合運動場, 駒沢通り, 駒沢公園, 深沢, 世田谷区

records.name: Baji Koen (Tokyo Equestrian Park)
records.description: An equestrian sports venue owned by the Japan Racing Association, functioning as a public park year-round and known locally as 'Horse Park.' Originally built for the cancelled 1940 Olympics, it hosted equestrian events for the 2020 Tokyo Olympics after a 2016-2023 renovation, during which operations were temporarily relocated to Utsunomiya.
